metadata.title: SSPP Template - Institutional Identity Federation (SSO)
metadata.remarks: Normative SSPP template defining institutional requirements for federated authentication, authorization enforcement, and conditional access using a centrally governed identity federation service. This SSPP establishes trust boundaries, assurance expectations, and governance obligations for all SSO-integrated services, independent of vendor or protocol.

props.name: implements-architecture-pattern
props.remarks: This SSPP implements the institutional Identity Federation architecture pattern.

import-profile.remarks: Imports institutional baseline security, identity, and access governance requirements.

system-characteristics.system-description: A centrally governed identity federation service providing authentication and single sign-on for institutional users and applications. The service consumes and issues federated identity assertions, enforces authentication and access policy, and integrates with institutional monitoring and audit capabilities.

props.name: institutional-owner
props.remarks: Owns identity lifecycle, federation trust relationships, and access governance.

props.name: technical-owner
props.remarks: Defines and enforces authentication standards, assurance requirements, and conditional access controls.

props.name: identity-federation-model
props.remarks: A centralized federation broker mediates trust, policy, and assurance between users, applications, and external identity providers.

props.name: governance-model
props.remarks: Federation trust relationships, authentication policies, and access controls are centrally governed. Delegation is limited and explicitly controlled.

props.name: authentication-model
props.remarks: Applications rely on federated authentication rather than managing credentials locally.

props.name: supported-protocols
props.remarks: Common federation and modern authentication protocols. Protocol choice does not alter governance expectations.

props.name: multi-factor-authentication
props.remarks: Multi-factor authentication is required for all interactive user authentication in accordance with institutional policy.

props.name: conditional-access
props.remarks: Risk-based access decisions incorporate user, device, location, and session context.

props.name: coarse-grained-access-control
props.remarks: Access to an application MUST be restricted at the federation service using explicit application assignment or equivalent controls.

props.name: fine-grained-authorization
props.remarks: Fine-grained authorization SHOULD be enforced using centrally governed groups or attributes. Service-internal role models are permitted but increase governance and attestation risk.

props.name: claims-governance
props.remarks: Federated assertions include only approved, minimal claims necessary for access and authorization decisions.

props.name: federation-trust-lifecycle
props.remarks: Federation trust creation, modification, and removal require formal approval and documented justification.

props.name: non-interactive-identities
props.remarks: Service principals, workload identities, and non-interactive authentication are governed under separate institutional identity standards.

props.name: logging-and-audit
props.remarks: Authentication, federation, and conditional access decisions are logged centrally and treated as authoritative audit records.

system-implementation.remarks: This SSPP defines institutional identity federation requirements and control expectations. Application-specific federation configurations, claim mappings, and authorization models are documented in SSPP instances. This SSPP inherits trust, assurance, and responsibility boundary requirements from the Identity Federation architecture pattern.

components.title: Identity Federation Core Services
components.description: Federation service providing authentication, assertion issuance and consumption, and policy enforcement.

components.title: Conditional Access and Assurance Enforcement
components.description: Enforces assurance and access policy based on contextual risk signals.

components.title: Federated Identity Logging and Monitoring
components.description: Centralized logging of federated authentication and access decisions.

links.text: Federation and access events are forwarded to the institutional SIEM.

roles.title: Identity Policy Authority
roles.remarks: Defines federation posture, assurance requirements, and acceptable use of externally asserted identities.

roles.title: Identity Architect
roles.remarks: Designs federation patterns, trust boundaries, and integration models.

roles.title: Identity Operations
roles.remarks: Operates the federation service and enforces centrally defined controls.

roles.title: Identity Monitoring and Assessment
roles.remarks: Monitors federated authentication activity and supports audit, investigations, and risk assessments.

control-implementation.remarks: Control satisfaction is achieved through enforced federated authentication, mandatory MFA, conditional access, minimized claims, centrally governed authorization, and authoritative logging. Detailed control inheritance is documented through the imported institutional baseline and the Identity Federation architecture pattern.
